name: Georgism
summary: Georgism, from the American economist Henry George, holds that people own what they produce but that land and natural resources belong to everyone, so the rent they yield should go to the community. Its main policy is a tax on the unimproved value of land that would replace taxes on labor, capital and trade, leaving land in private hands while socializing its rent. It pairs this with free trade and opposition to monopoly privilege, and some adherents would return surplus rent as a citizen's dividend.
scope: Classical Georgism as set out in Henry George's Progress and Poverty (1879) and the single-tax movement, together with the mainstream of modern geoism and geolibertarianism (land value tax advocates). Social questions George never addressed are inferred from the movement's classical-liberal outlook and marked low confidence. Excludes the anarchist offshoots of Nock and Heath and the proprietary-community ideas of Spencer MacCallum.

universal-healthcare.rationale: George never addressed healthcare; social-democratic Georgists would fund it from land rent while geolibertarians would not, so adherents are split.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Georgists hold that wages are pushed down by land monopoly and rise once rent is socialized, so they look to the land tax rather than wage mandates; inferred from George's theory of wages and free-market leanings.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: George accepted free competition and private capital and blamed poverty on land monopoly and privilege rather than on markets, so markets are trusted once land rent is public.

public-ownership.rationale: George favored municipal ownership of utilities and transit as natural monopolies, but modern geolibertarians reject it and the movement was divided, with many wanting only rights-of-way rents public.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Georgists want to abolish taxes on income, capital and produced wealth and tax only land values; they target unearned land rent, not wealth or high earners as such.

unions-good.rationale: George was a labor candidate (United Labor Party) and sympathetic to workers, though he held that only the land remedy could permanently raise wages; inferred from his labor alliances.

property-fundamental.rationale: Georgists treat property in the products of labor as sacrosanct but deny any natural right to land rent, so the general statement cuts both ways for them.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Georgists target legal privileges and monopolies but otherwise favor free enterprise; they prefer removing privileges and capturing rents over broad corporate regulation, so the general call is mixed.

cut-welfare.rationale: George proposed pensions and a citizen's dividend paid as a right rather than charity, and expected poverty to vanish under his remedy rather than through cutting support; inferred.

worker-ownership.rationale: George accepted private capital and wage labor and distinguished land from capital, rejecting socialist collective ownership of enterprise; the left later faulted his class collaborationism.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed by George; inferred from the movement's classical-liberal commitment to individual liberty and the civil-liberties causes later Georgists took up.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Inferred from the liberty-centered strand (Nock opposed Prohibition) and the movement's turn to civil liberties; not a stated core position.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Georgists of the Progressive era championed free speech and civil liberties; inferred for hate speech.

strong-leader.rationale: George was a democratic reformer who pushed the secret ballot and civil-service reform to curb abuses of power; inferred opposition to bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: George saw government becoming the administrator of a great cooperative society funded by rent, not something to abolish; anarchist Georgists like Nock are a minority.

limit-guns.rationale: Neither George nor modern Georgist organizations take a position on guns; the ideology is indifferent.

empower-police-military.rationale: George expected police, prisons and standing armies to shrink as poverty vanished, and he favored a smaller military.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Georgism's classical-liberal view that only rent and privilege, not voluntary exchange, are proper objects of state action.

decide-locally.rationale: The land value tax has mostly been pursued at city and state level, and Nock wanted it collected locally to starve the central state; inferred.

rehabilitation.rationale: George traced crime to poverty and expected his remedy to lighten the criminal law and its prisons; inferred for prison policy.

traditional-family.rationale: Georgism takes no position on family structure; the ideology is indifferent.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's liberal stance on personal liberty and George's support for women's suffrage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Georgism takes no position on abortion; though later Georgists backed birth control, the ideology is otherwise indifferent.

more-religion-public.rationale: George framed his case in moral and religious language but his views were deist and the program is secular; adherents are indifferent on this.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Georgism frames injustice around land monopoly rather than race and has no stated position; George himself held anti-Chinese views that later Georgists do not share.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Georgism takes no position on the nature of gender.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The program is economic and universal; it takes no position on national culture.

gradual-change.rationale: George proposed working through the existing tax machinery, leaving titles in owners' hands and abolishing other taxes step by step rather than confiscating land.

reduce-immigration.rationale: George opposed Chinese immigration in 1869, but modern Georgists' free-trade, equal-access principles point toward openness; answered for the current mainstream and inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Georgism has no stated view on international organizations.

free-trade.rationale: Free trade was a core plank: George wrote Protection or Free Trade and the movement's slogan was 'Free Trade, Free Land, Free Men'.

nation-first.rationale: Georgists' universal free-trade stance and George's anti-militarism point away from national self-interest over cooperation; inferred.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: George expected standing armies to disappear and wanted a smaller military; isolationist Georgists such as Chodorov opposed foreign wars; inferred.

open-borders.rationale: Free trade and equal rights to land suggest openness, but George himself backed immigration restriction and modern Georgists are not committed to open borders; split.

limit-growth.rationale: Georgists expect the land tax to unleash production and treat pollution as a rent to be charged, not growth as something to cap; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Modern Georgists count the atmosphere as land and favor auctioning pollution rights or cap-and-share with the rent going to the public; how drastic is contested.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The thesis of Progress and Poverty is that rising productive power cannot permanently benefit the masses while land is privately monopolized.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Georgism has no position on nuclear power.

revolution-justified.rationale: George sought change through elections and tax reform rather than revolution, and the radical left rejected his reformism; inferred.

experts-over-public.rationale: George was a democratic campaigner who relied on popular persuasion and the ballot; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: George explicitly preferred private possession and free competition, achieving socialism's aims 'without coercion' rather than by state direction of the economy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Georgists accept private ownership of businesses and capital; only land rent is to be socialized.

land-value-tax.rationale: Replacing other taxes with a tax on land values is the defining Georgist policy: 'abolish all taxation save that upon land values'.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Georgists oppose taxing produced wealth, and George let landholders bequeath their holdings while public revenue came from rent alone.

basic-income.rationale: George proposed a citizen's dividend funded by land rent, and many modern Georgists back a rent-funded dividend, though others prefer tax cuts.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: George argued tariffs raise prices, protect monopolies and do not lift wages; anti-protectionism is central to the movement.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Georgists want the state to collect rent and fund public goods, leaving investment decisions to private enterprise.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Georgists expect the land tax to break up speculative holdings and give everyone access to land, but they do not oppose corporations as such; inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Georgism accepts money, markets and wage labor; George's concern was that land monopoly depresses wages, not wages themselves.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: George favored state-issued debt-free money like the greenback and opposed privately created money, the opposite of free banking.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Georgists rely on free markets once land rent is public, not state-organized wage and price setting; inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: George worked through competitive elections and reforms like the secret ballot; scholars describe his utopia as liberal democracy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Georgism grew up in American republican and democratic reform politics; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: George championed the secret ballot and women's suffrage, and his historian concludes his utopia was liberal democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Progressive-era Georgists campaigned for democratic reforms alongside the single tax; inferred from that reform tradition.

workers-councils.rationale: Georgism works through parliaments and local government and rejects class-based politics.

right-to-secede.rationale: Georgism takes no position on secession beyond some anarchist strands; indifferent.

natural-rulers.rationale: George's egalitarian case rests on all people's equal right to the earth; inferred.

political-violence-never.rationale: George was a peaceful reformer but did not state a pacifist doctrine; no settled position.

war-builds-character.rationale: George expected standing armies to disappear as society improved and favored a smaller military; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: George's deist outlook and the movement's secular reform program point to separation; inferred.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Georgist law rests on natural rights and economics rather than scripture, despite George's moral rhetoric; inferred.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Mainstream Georgism sees government as a rent-funded cooperative administrator; privatized-governance ideas (Heath, MacCallum) are a breakaway strand.

military-superiority.rationale: George favored reducing the military and expected standing armies to vanish.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Georgism's claim that every person has an equal right to the earth is universal; George's anti-Chinese views are not held by the modern movement. Inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: George blamed poverty on land monopoly, not on a capital-labor conflict, and the socialist left rejected him for class collaborationism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Georgists seek equal access to natural opportunities while letting each keep what they produce, which is equality of opportunity rather than of outcome.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Georgism holds land rent belongs to all, which conflicts with exclusive group authority, but it has no settled position on indigenous lands.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Georgism takes no position on colonial reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Georgism is universalist and has no place for religious or civilizational blocs; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: George appealed to both individual liberty and moral duty to others; Georgism takes no clear stance on egoism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Georgism grounds its case in individual rights to one's labor and equal rights to land; inferred.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Georgists treat nature as a common inheritance whose rent belongs to all, not as having intrinsic value; some ecological Georgists go further. Split.

limit-population.rationale: George rejected the Malthusian view that population outruns subsistence, blaming poverty on land monopoly instead; inferred for policy.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: George admired material progress and blamed its failure to relieve poverty on land monopoly, not industry.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on the pace of technological change.

human-enhancement.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on human enhancement.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on algorithmic government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on encryption.

restore-past-order.rationale: George's program is framed as progress toward a just society, not restoration; inferred.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Georgists argue from both natural-rights principle and economic efficiency; there is no settled stance on this.

direct-action.rationale: George pursued his program through electoral campaigns, including his runs for mayor of New York, and through tax legislation rather than strikes or extra-parliamentary action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Georgism has no stated doctrine on whether methods must prefigure the goal; its peaceful, legal methods follow from its reformism rather than from such a principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: George welcomed material progress and wanted its gains shared through the land tax, the opposite of abandoning settled, productive civilization.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Georgism's commitment to free trade and exchange presupposes specialization, and George blamed poverty on land monopoly rather than on the division of labor.

distribute-by-need.rationale: George held that each person has a right to what their labor produces; only land rent is shared, so distribution follows work rather than need.

production-for-use.rationale: Georgists accept private enterprise and markets once land rent is socialized; production for profit is not their target, so they reject replacing it.

profit-exploitation.rationale: George located the injustice in land rent, not in returns to capital, and the socialist left rejected his program for refusing to treat capital as exploiting labor.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Georgism rejects class-based politics and aims at liberal democracy, so a class dictatorship is foreign to it.

collective-farming.rationale: George's remedy explicitly leaves land in private possession and takes only its rent, so individual farmers keep working their own holdings.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: George traced war to the struggle over land and to protectionism rather than to capitalism as such; inferred from his account of land and his free-trade case.

taxation-theft.rationale: George called taxes on earnings, occupations, investments and buildings infringements of the right of property that 'take by force what belongs to the individual alone', but he held that collecting land rent is not theft, since rent belongs to the community.

harm-principle.rationale: Not stated in these terms; inferred from the movement's classical-liberal outlook and its defense of civil liberties.

individual-rights-only.rationale: George grounded his case in each individual's right to the fruits of their labor and each person's equal right to land, not in group rights; inferred.

conscription.rationale: George wanted a smaller military and expected standing armies to fade; inferred from that and from his view that a person's labor is their own.

exit-over-voice.rationale: George relied on the ballot and democratic reform, such as the secret ballot, rather than exit, to check government; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: George pictured government as the administrator of a cooperative society funded by common rent, not as a firm with customers; the proprietary-community strand is outside this audit's scope.

media-academia-power.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on the power of universities or the press.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Georgism takes no position on genetic group differences; George's anti-Chinese views of 1869 are not held by the modern movement.

organic-representation.rationale: George campaigned through political parties and elections and backed the secret ballot and suffrage, not corporate or family representation; inferred.

total-state.rationale: George wanted to 'simplify and reduce' government machinery and achieve socialism's aims without coercion, the opposite of a state directing all of life.

national-rebirth.rationale: Georgism is a universal economic program, not a call for national regeneration; inferred.

territorial-expansion.rationale: George favored free trade and a smaller military and saw the struggle for land as a source of war; inferred.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Georgism rests on equal natural rights and democratic government; inferred from that outlook.

bound-labor.rationale: George compared private property in land to slavery and held that each worker owns their labor and its fruits, so binding farmers to a lord contradicts the ideology's core.

universal-morality.rationale: George argued from a natural and moral law that holds for all people, deriving property in labor and equal rights to land from it.

single-common-good.rationale: George presented the land tax as serving all classes rather than as a deal between interests, and was criticized by socialists for class collaboration; inferred.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on a Jewish state; its universal program is indifferent to it.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on diaspora return rights.

revive-national-language.rationale: Georgism has no stated position on national languages.

workplace-democracy.rationale: George never proposed codetermination; he left firms privately run and expected wages to rise once land rent is socialized, so this is inferred from his theory and is low confidence.

school-vouchers.rationale: George did not address vouchers; inferred that geolibertarians favor school choice while social-democratic Georgists defend public schooling, so adherents are split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: George did not discuss Keynesian stimulus; inferred from his aim of funding government from land rent and his general distrust of privilege and burdens on producers, at low confidence.

economic-freedom.rationale: George argued that political liberty is hollow while land monopoly leaves workers economically dependent, so he agrees freedom needs economic freedom, though he means equal access to land rather than laissez-faire alone.

rule-by-example.rationale: George expected social order to come from reforming institutions (taxing land rent) and removing the causes of crime, not from rulers' example; inferred from his view of government as cooperative administration.

national-self-determination.rationale: George never made this a central theme; inferred from the movement's classical-liberal outlook, which favors self-government and free trade between peoples over imperial rule, so a modest agree.

force-without-un.rationale: George favored a smaller military and expected standing armies to vanish, and isolationist Georgists opposed foreign wars, while the movement favors cooperation between peoples; inferred.

reason-over-faith.rationale: George argued from natural rights and political economy but framed his case in religious terms, appealing to the Creator's equal gift of the earth; inferred from that blend, as he never ruled out faith as a guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: George's pensions and citizen's dividend were framed as a share of common land rent owed to members of the community as a right, and he never proposed tying benefits to citizenship; modern Georgists' free-trade, equal-access principles lean against reserving benefits for citizens, though George's own 1869 anti-Chinese-immigration stance and the dividend's 'citizen' framing leave this split. Inferred, not directly sourced.

positive-liberty.rationale: George held that denying people access to land denies them the means to live and act freely, and left-libertarian readings of him treat common ownership of resources as a condition of real freedom; inferred from that.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Georgists blame poverty on land monopoly rather than idleness and some favour an unconditional citizen's dividend from rent; inferred from that, with geolibertarians opposed to welfare altogether.

class-collaboration.rationale: Georgism is described as class-collaborationist: it holds that labor and capital are allies against landowners and rent-takers, not opposed classes.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inferred from George's classical-liberal, civilization-building outlook; he never proposed sweeping away cultural institutions.

dominated-front.rationale: Inferred from George's free-trade internationalism, which favoured open dealings between nations rather than hostile blocs.

workers-nation.rationale: Inferred from George's free trade and appeal to common interests across classes rather than national class organization; he did oppose some immigration, so this is not strong.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: George supported women's suffrage and equal rights under law, and the movement's liberal outlook treats public roles as open to all.

ban-interest.rationale: George treated interest as the natural return to productive capital, distinct from rent, and left capital untaxed and free; only land rent is to be collected.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Georgism rests on equal natural rights to land for all people and a liberal-democratic state, which is incompatible with legal racial classification; inferred from that.

state-class-instrument.rationale: George saw government as captured by monopoly interests but held it could be reformed into cooperative administration by removing privilege, rejecting the view that the state is inherently a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Not a George-era issue; inferred from the Georgist view that extraction rent and pollution should be charged to the holder, which favours taxing rather than promoting extraction.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal tolerance and George's free-trade, individual-liberty outlook, which does not demand surrendering one's culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: Inferred: George traced social ills to land monopoly and privilege, an impersonal economic mechanism, not to a plot to displace a population.

proportional-representation.rationale: Inferred from George's support for ballot and electoral reform and the movement's democratic-liberal outlook; no direct statement was found.

national-mission.rationale: Inferred from George's picture of government as cooperative administration and his pacific, free-trade internationalism, with no mission to export a system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: George backed women's suffrage but the movement did not develop a theory of systemic male advantage; adherents are split.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: George argued that privilege and land monopoly corrupt government, so adherents tend to see political elites as serving entrenched interests; inferred.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Inferred from George's equal-rights and individual-liberty principles, which leave no room for state control of reproduction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Inferred from the movement's civil-liberties and equal-rights tradition and its distrust of armed state power.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Georgists want the state to collect rent and often run natural monopolies and utilities, so they reject a strictly minimal state, though they favour a small one.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Georgism is an economic doctrine that says nothing on intermarriage; its liberal individualism implies marriage is a private choice.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: George's remedy rests on the equal right of every person to land and to the earth's gifts, which implies equal standing before the law.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Georgism seeks reform of land and taxation by democratic means, not revolution, and George rejected socialism; the statement is inferred as one adherents would not endorse.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: George never addressed settler states as such; adherents are split between seeing displacement as land monopoly and seeing it as ordinary history.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from classical-liberal equality before the law; George did not address personal-law systems.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal outlook of the movement, which favours freedom of religion; George did not discuss conversion law.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Inferred: a ban restricts economic and personal liberty and is not part of the land-rent programme.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal secularism; George's own view on school religion is not documented in the sources, and some adherents differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Inferred from the movement's distrust of state power and George's aim of reducing government to its minimum functions.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Inferred from the democratic and natural-rights tradition George wrote in; he did not frame legitimacy this way directly.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: George treated political economy and natural law as objective truths found by reason; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Georgists hold that tariffs raise prices and protect monopoly and that free trade benefits all; a trade surplus as goal is the protectionist view they reject.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal commitment to individual rights and its opposition to privilege; no source addresses it.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: George called taxes on the products of labor force against rightful property; geolibertarians agree strongly while social Georgists accept coercive rent collection, so inferred as moderately agree.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: George held that progress comes from association and cooperation under equal rights, and blamed monopoly rather than lack of competition for poverty; inferred.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Georgists of the Progressive era championed civil liberties and free speech; inferred for banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: George held that land monopoly gives owners power over those who must use the land, which fits an arbitrary-power view of unfreedom; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: George's utopia was a liberal democracy with ballot reform, and he did not seek concentrated power; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: George sought change through elections and tax reform and rejected revolutionary leadership; inferred.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The remedy was aimed at ending poverty by securing equal rights to land, though framed as equal rights rather than priority for the poor; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Georgists want land rent shared but accept private possession; George never addressed public housing, and adherents would split on a windfall of land value to tenants.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: George backed labour organisation but opposed coercion and favoured freeing labour through land reform; inferred, so restrictions on strikes are mildly opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: George attacked the Malthusian claim directly, arguing poverty comes from private monopoly of land rather than from too many people.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: George held that more people raise wealth and favoured open immigration on principle; inferred that diversity is not seen as a threat to cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: George pressed for ballot reform and elected, accountable government; lotteries are not part of the tradition and are inferred to be disfavoured.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The classical-liberal outlook of the movement is inferred to hold that legal protections should stand; George never addressed emergency powers.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Georgists favour free trade and untaxed markets, with monopoly rent as the target rather than prices; inferred opposition to ceilings.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from George's liberal, anti-privilege outlook; he never proposed state or party control of information.

party-commands-army.rationale: George expected government to shrink and armies to dwindle under the single tax; party command of the army is inferred to be alien to this.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: George favoured open immigration and the movement is liberal on migration; inferred that long residence requirements are disfavoured.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: George wanted cheap, honest government but never addressed pay for office; inferred and adherents vary.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: George campaigned for ballot reform against party machines and ran as an independent, so he favored individual judgment over binding party lines; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: George backed free trade and was cosmopolitan, but he did not propose pooled sovereignty, so adherents are split; inferred.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Georgism envisions democratic cooperative administration with reduced police and armies, so a strong executive over the military runs against it.

church-by-bishops.rationale: George wrote to the Pope as a moral critic and had no program for church governance; adherents are indifferent.

clerical-rule.rationale: Georgism is a liberal-democratic movement that held power should rest on equal rights of citizens, and George did not seek clerical government.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: George saw wars as growing from land struggles and opposed militarism, but did not preach defeatism; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The movement sided with civil liberties and a classical-liberal outlook, which weighs against state censorship of art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: George did not address term limits and classical liberals disagree on them; adherents are split.

recall-officials.rationale: Georgists supported direct-democracy reforms such as the initiative and referendum in the Progressive era; inferred for recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred: George opposed imperial adventures and tariffs and favoured peaceful free trade, so entangling permanent alliances sit poorly with the outlook; the movement has no stated alliance policy.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Georgism leaves land in private possession and taxes its rent, so it keeps tenancy and ownership as ordinary arrangements; it targets land monopoly, not renting.

people-in-arms.rationale: Never addressed; classical-liberal wariness of standing armies is offset by acceptance of ordinary state defence, so adherents are split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Inferred: George blamed rent speculation for urban squalor and held that reform would let cities flourish, rather than praising rural life as morally better.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National borders and partition are outside Georgist doctrine; the movement is genuinely indifferent.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Inferred: George addressed workers and the common reader and respected ordinary experience, but nothing in the doctrine casts the educated as out of touch.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Inferred: George rejected racial theories of social difference, yet shared the 19th-century faith in progress; adherents are split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the humanitarian, classical-liberal outlook of the movement. Contested among adherents.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from George's support for public schooling, equal rights and women's suffrage; the movement set no specific curriculum position.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Inferred: Georgists favoured secular, science-based public schooling and classical-liberal limits on state promotion of doctrine.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal and libertarian-leaning side of the movement, which opposes censorship of adults.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred: Georgism's equal-rights principle and the liberal tradition of birthright citizenship favour citizenship by birth on the territory.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; geolibertarians would leave languages to individuals while social-democratic Georgists might fund them, so adherents are split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Inferred from the principle of equal rights under one law, which Georgists apply to land and taxes alike.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal, individual-liberty strand that George drew on and libertarian Georgists carry on.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred: Georgism holds that legitimate claims rest on earned property, and it offers land rent rather than repudiation as the remedy.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: George holds that political progress cannot benefit the masses while land is monopolized; applied to independence, an inference.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Not addressed; Georgists favor democratic reform but have no position on constitution-making procedure.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: George sought socialism's goals without coercion and champions liberty; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Georgists stress removing monopoly privilege and free trade over charity; inferred and contested among social-democratic adherents.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Inferred from George's expectation that armies and police would shrink as justice spreads.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from George's democratic and ballot-reform positions.

central-bank-independence.rationale: No stated position; geolibertarians distrust central banks while social-democratic Georgists do not, so adherents are split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from George's free trade, anti-war outlook and view that land belongs to all rather than to a nation's claim.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Land is common property held subject to paying its rent to the community, though George treats the product of labor as fully private.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: George died before the USSR, and Georgists generally contrast their voluntary approach with coercive socialism; inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Inferred from the view that natural resources belong to everyone, which supports protecting them from harm.

collective-defense.rationale: George addressed trade and peace but not alliances; adherents have no settled view.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal, equal-rights outlook that rejects rule without consent.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: George's open letter to Pope Leo XIII engages the Church respectfully, and the classical-liberal outlook opposes state seizure of property apart from land rent.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's focus was fiscal reform, not the form of the head of state.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal consent-based outlook and opposition to coercion.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Inferred from the movement's support for local self-government and its small land-tax enclaves.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Inferred from George's insistence on equal natural rights for all, which excludes divinely descended rulers.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Georgists would abolish taxes on labor in favor of a land value tax, so even a flat income tax is a tax on earnings they oppose.

character-from-environment.rationale: George argued that poverty and vice come from institutions such as land monopoly, not from human nature.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Inferred from the equal-rights and classical-liberal outlook, which subjects rulers to law.

space-expansion.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is about land and rent and has no common view of space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not addressed by George; adherents split between democratic and liberal-constitutional views.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from the equal-rights and classical-liberal outlook, which opposes the veneration of rulers.

equal-parenting.rationale: Not addressed; the movement had no stated position on custody and adherents are split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: George held that land reform could end poverty without class war, and aimed at socialism's goals without coercion; the claim is inferred as unaddressed.

land-redistribution.rationale: George held it unnecessary to confiscate land and proposed leaving it in private possession while taking its rent through a tax.

refugee-return.rationale: Inferred from George's equal-rights principle; refugee return was not addressed.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred: George's free-trade, anti-privilege outlook is cosmopolitan and not nationalist.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal outlook of the movement; George did not address it.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal outlook of the movement; George did not address it.

common-currency.rationale: George's views on money are documented but a multinational currency was not addressed, and geolibertarians and social Georgists differ.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred: George's free-trade internationalism has no place for ethnic-kin unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred: the movement's individualist, classical-liberal outlook favours no state-sponsored group institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Inferred from George's equal-rights principle and belief in reform through democratic politics.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: George held that ideas and institutions such as land tenure, not an autonomous economic process, shape society, and urged moral reform.

ban-cartels.rationale: George opposed monopoly privilege, though his remedy was removing privilege and taxing rent, not breaking up firms by prohibition.

no-bailouts.rationale: Inferred: the free-market, anti-privilege outlook rejects public rescue of failing firms.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: George was a democrat who backed ballot reform, but the movement's classical-liberal strand favours limits on majorities.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: George backed women's suffrage, but quotas were not addressed and the classical-liberal outlook opposes mandated parity.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Free trade is a core Georgist position, so a bloc shut off from outside trade is opposed.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred from the free-trade stance, which opposes binding conditions on trade agreements.

moral-incentives.rationale: George's economics treats the removal of rent-taking and taxes as the way to prosperity, not a replacement of material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: George sought reform by persuasion and the ballot, so armed vanguards are opposed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred: Georgism targets unearned privilege and holds that no one should gain by monopoly or birth.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Inferred from George's universalist, free-trade classical liberalism, which does not centre one nation's story.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Inferred: George opposed monopoly privilege and the equal-rights basis of his thought cuts against rule over other peoples.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from George's liberal individualism, which gives no special role to teaching national loyalty.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Inferred from George's equal-rights principle that privileges should not be granted by law to any group.

public-money-creation.rationale: George's writings on money are varied and adherents are split on who should issue it; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: George held that poverty arises from land monopoly and can be cured by reform, not collapse; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Inferred from George's anti-monopoly, free-trade outlook, which has no place for imperial influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Georgists champion free trade, so poor countries are urged to open up, not break ties.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Georgists attribute low wages to land monopoly within each country, not to extraction from poor countries; inferred.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Geolibertarians would allow it while social Georgists stress equal rights; adherents are split.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Inferred from George's defence of property in labour and civil liberties against the state.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed by George or Georgists; adherents split on historical treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: George championed democratic government, ballot reform and wide suffrage and opposed privilege, so election over inheritance is implied.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from George's democratic majoritarianism; not stated.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Inferred from George's democratic and classical-liberal outlook; he did not state it as a doctrine.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from George's democratic outlook; the question of parliament versus monarch was not his.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: George and his movement did not address animal welfare; adherents are split.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the common nineteenth-century and liberal view.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: George argued justice rather than charity, in The Condition of Labor and elsewhere, and rejected paternalist benevolence.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: George was a reformer who stood for office and organized a political movement, and held politics a duty.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from George's faith in popular democracy and free discussion; not stated.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: George emphasized monopoly privilege and law, but not culture or hegemony; the sources do not address it.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: George attributed poverty to land monopoly and favoured free trade, which is not the structural-transfer view.

native-born-offices.rationale: George opposed Chinese exclusion in places but favoured citizenship by residence; inferred and weakly sourced.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Free trade and land reform are the Georgist route to development, rather than aid; inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: George opposed militarism and conquest, and the movement favoured free trade and peace; inferred.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from equal-rights liberalism, though Georgists sympathize with indigenous land claims.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Georgism predates fascism; modern adherents are split.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal and geolibertarian outlook, which often condemns all totalitarian systems alike.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: George was an abolitionist-era Republican liberal who saw slavery as the cause; inferred, not stated in the sources.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between social-democratic and libertarian views.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Georgists hold that equal rights to land are universal, which implies universal principles; inferred.

military-guardian-role.rationale: George wanted police and armies to shrink and opposed militarism, and held that government should be cooperative administration.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from the preference for ending taxes on labour and leaving wages to free markets; adherents split.

filial-duty.rationale: George never addressed it; inferred from the classical-liberal outlook that family duties are voluntary rather than enforced.

office-by-exam.rationale: George supported democratic reforms such as the secret ballot; appointment by examination is not a Georgist theme, so inferred from his democratic outlook.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Georgists favour free trade and no barriers to commerce, so blocking foreign purchases of firms conflicts with it.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Not addressed by George; inferred from the liberal and individual-liberty outlook of the movement.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Inferred from George's support for direct democratic reforms and the later single-tax movement's alliance with direct legislation; not directly sourced.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: George proposed paying pensions from surplus land rent rather than private accounts; individual accounts are inferred as not a Georgist programme.

land-use-tenure.rationale: George said land belongs equally to all but left it in private possession, secure and saleable, taxing its rent; this is neither common tenure by use nor outright idle ownership.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Inferred from George's democratic constitutionalism and government by cooperative administration of public revenue.

single-official-language.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's classical-liberal, anti-coercive outlook.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Georgists hold land to be the equal birthright of all people and favour free trade; a citizen-only land rule is inferred as foreign to that universal claim.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal outlook that equal treatment concerns rules, not outcomes; George did not address the question.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: George attacked waste and luxury from monopoly wealth but defended free markets; adherents are not united, and he did not address consumerism as such.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: George's writing looked to shrinking police and armies and peaceful cooperation; arming foreign rebels is inferred as contrary to it.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from George's hostility to large armies and coercive government and his free-trade internationalism.

corporate-influence.rationale: George attacked monopoly privilege and its hold on lawmaking; inferred that adherents would oppose business capture of government.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Georgists favour free trade and open exchange; inferred opposition to state screening of foreign money.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: George rejected the Malthusian population problem but proposed no state birth incentives; inferred from his reliance on land reform, not subsidies, to end want.

residents-only-property.rationale: George held that all have an equal right to land, so reserving local land for residents cuts against that; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: George held that opening land by taxing its rent would give everyone work, so no state employer of last resort is needed; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: George's expectation of shrinking armies and cooperative government, and the movement's free-trade internationalism, point to support; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Georgists are split: geolibertarians reject political obligation while the liberal-democratic mainstream treats law as legitimate.

non-intervention.rationale: George and the movement opposed tariffs and imperial entanglement; inferred support for non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: George held that unions cannot cure poverty while land is monopolised and took no side on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Georgism was a liberal reform movement blaming land monopoly, not minorities; a conspiracy claim has no place in it.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: George never addressed it; the liberal outlook treats marriage as a settled institution, though libertarian adherents lean the other way.

public-access-to-information.rationale: George backed ballot reform and open democratic government; inferred support for a legal right to government information.

local-production.rationale: Georgists champion free trade and a division of labour across distance, so goods should come from wherever they are cheapest.

informal-organisation.rationale: The single-tax movement organised through leagues and campaigns for a legislated reform; inferred rejection of purely informal groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Georgism leans cosmopolitan and free-trading; inferred that national law should not have the last word over international law.

religious-nation.rationale: George grounded rights in natural law and equal claims to land, not in a national faith; inferred.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: George favoured free trade and a shrinking state and army, so tribute and ritual submission between states is inferred to be foreign to the movement.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Georgists want land rent to fund local government, but George also backed a common dividend and nothing in the sources settles pooling across regions, so adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Georgists hold that people own what they produce while land is common, which implies private personal belongings, though they reject common ownership of all productive tools.

defeat-communism.rationale: George rejected socialism of the state-ownership kind but never framed it as an enemy to be defeated, and the movement has no settled foreign policy on it.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: George backed public ownership of natural monopolies such as utilities while Georgist libertarians prefer private provision, so adherents are split.

religion-illusion.rationale: George wrote from a religious conviction about natural justice and equal rights, so the view that religion is a consoling illusion is inferred to be rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: George credited industrial progress with great wealth but argued land monopoly turns it into poverty, so adherents would not call capitalism a simple foundation for better society.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: George backed women suffrage, and Georgists hold that land reform would raise all wages, but the movement is split on whether further economic transformation is needed.

socialized-care.rationale: Georgism is classical-liberal in outlook and never proposed public kitchens or nurseries, so socialised domestic work is inferred to be rejected.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred from the movement free-trade and classical-liberal outlook, which treats language as free exchange and has no tradition of official purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the respect for property and natural rights in the movement, which favours keeping lasting agreements, though George never addressed treaties with internal nations.

cooperative-communities.rationale: George wanted land rent taxed within existing states and markets rather than a society of small communal-property communities, though some single-tax enclaves existed.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the free-trade, anti-privilege outlook, which opposes state steering of where groups live.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: George presented land reform as a remedy distinct from both laissez-faire and socialism, and later Georgists describe it as a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: George held that every generation has an equal right to the earth, so ancient claims cannot outweigh present people.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the movement's classical-liberal commitment to truth and human rights.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: George never addressed it; inferred from the liberal outlook of the movement, which opposes punishing private conduct.

suppress-opposition.rationale: George held that free speech and free political competition are essential, and the movement is classical liberal.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: George was religious but argued from natural rights and equal liberty, not state enforcement of faith.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Georgists favor free trade and oppose privilege and monopoly, which colonial exploitation embodies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: a classical-liberal, non-Islamic movement that does not see religious duty as a basis for war.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: Georgists rest legitimacy on equal rights, not religious law, and favor peaceful reform.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from democratic reformers to geolibertarians who distrust collective decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: George traced poverty and inequality chiefly to land monopoly, so Georgists tend to treat them as separable from other forms of oppression.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; adherents are split between liberal and libertarian leanings.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal emphasis on individual liberty over one's own life.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Georgists commonly claim to combine free markets with social ownership of land rent, which draws on both sides.

alienated-labor.rationale: George held that labor earns its product and is robbed by rent, not alienated by wage work itself; inferred from his theory.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal universalism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: George saw land as the Creator's gift to all, but he grounded government in equal rights and consent; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would split between neutrality of the state and liberty of dress.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; classical liberals value freedom of contract while others favor access to courts, so adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: Split: Georgists want free markets with land rent taken for the public, but social-democratic Georgists add social protection and geolibertarians would not.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: George wanted peace and free trade but not unilateral disarmament; geolibertarians favor limited defence.

rich-first.rationale: George argued that progress under land monopoly produces poverty alongside wealth, so letting some rise first at others' cost is the problem.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from George's free trade and opposition to militarism and entangling rivalries.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred: George was a democratic republican who attacked hereditary privilege, but he did not address succession of heads of state.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred: George held that interest is a natural return to capital and wanted freed markets in credit, not a mutualist system of interest-free credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: George never addressed international lenders; free-trade Georgists oppose conditionality as state interference, while others accept sound-finance conditions.

property-franchise.rationale: George campaigned for equal political rights and democracy, and Georgists oppose privilege based on wealth.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred: George backed women's suffrage, but his thought treats land and nature as an economic resource to be shared, not as a joint logic of domination.

reification.rationale: Inferred: Georgists see markets as just once land monopoly is removed, rejecting the Marxist claim that markets distort social perception.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred: Georgists locate the injustice in land monopoly rather than in private ownership of presses, and value formal freedoms in a classical-liberal outlook.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal outlook and opposition to privilege; George did not discuss rule by decree directly.

racial-franchise.rationale: George stood for equal rights and attacked privilege; Georgism's equal-rights-to-land principle has no place for racial limits on the franchise.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic: George wrote long before the internet, and the movement has no settled view on online deliberation.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred: land value taxation relies on public valuation records and Georgists favour transparent assessment, but the movement has no stated position on open data generally.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal outlook and equal-rights principle; George never addressed it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred: singling out businesses by owners' religion contradicts equal rights and free trade, though George never addressed it.

citizens-assembly.rationale: George backed ballot reform and popular government, but sortition was never part of Georgism; inferred from his democratic outlook, adherents have no shared view.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: George wrote as a Christian moral reformer who read religious ethics against the Church's social conservatism in his open letter to Leo XIII; inferred that he favoured rethinking inherited teaching, low confidence.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: George held that land monopoly concentrates wealth and power and that progress cannot benefit the masses while land is monopolized, though Georgists target land rent rather than wealth as such.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by George; inferred from the movement's liberal stance on personal liberty and equal rights.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Inferred: George's thought rests on natural rights and equal liberty under one law, and he wrote as a religious moral reformer, so state promotion of atheism is rejected.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: George expected police and prisons to shrink as poverty vanished, but he did not propose abolishing them.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from equal individual rights under common law; George did not address communal power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: George held that poverty results from land monopoly and is cured by justice in land, not by charity, which he saw as treating symptoms.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed by George; adherents are indifferent or split between reformers favouring and opposing term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; George favoured ballot reform and direct democracy tools of the Progressive era, but delegable voting is anachronistic.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; George was a 19th-century thinker concerned with poverty, and adherents have no common view on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from George's support for women's suffrage and the movement's liberal equal-rights outlook; not addressed for religious office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from George's support for women's suffrage and the movement's equal-rights outlook; marriage was not addressed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal, free-trade outlook and George's equal-rights-to-land principle, which is not tied to nationality; George did not address local voting.

rent-control.rationale: Georgists hold that housing costs come from land monopoly and favour taxing land values rather than capping rents, which they expect to cut supply.

abolish-ip.rationale: George defended rewards to labour and invention but attacked monopoly privilege, and later Georgists split on patents and copyright.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: George wanted government shrunk to cooperative administration with smaller armies, which sits badly with drilled national-service youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from George's expectation that armies and police would shrink in a just society; nuclear basing was never addressed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Inferred from George's hope for peace, free trade and smaller armies, which point against foreign garrisons; never addressed directly.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Inferred: a liberal movement concerned with equal rights would support recognition of genocide, but George never addressed it.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: George's remedy exempts wages and the produce of labour from tax and takes land rent for the community, so income should come from work, not from holding land.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Georgism holds no pacifist doctrine and its classical-liberal outlook accepts defence of self and others; inferred.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred: Georgism is universalist and cosmopolitan in its free-trade and equal-rights outlook and gives no weight to national origin myths.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the classical-liberal outlook, which treats sex as natural and individual rights as universal; George did not address it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Georgism is individualist and indifferent to this feminist debate; adherents would not agree on it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred: George's critique of war and large armies is at odds with honouring death for the nation as sainthood.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: George wrote in strongly religious and moral terms about justice, as in his open letter to Pope Leo XIII, but modern adherents are secular and split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Georgism says nothing on diaspora and homelands; adherents have no common view.

culture-before-state.rationale: Georgism holds that fixing the land question comes first, as the root of poverty, so cultural renewal is not its priority; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: George was a Christian moralist, but modern Georgism takes no position on religious language; adherents are split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; adherents range from religious to secular and would not agree.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Georgism pairs free trade with opposition to privilege, and gives no group a claim on the economy; land rent goes to the whole community.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed; free trade and equal rights point away from ethnic territorial units, but there is no stated position.

independent-unions.rationale: George treated unions as legitimate voluntary associations in The Condition of Labor, and the movement's classical-liberal outlook favours organisations independent of the state; inferred.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: George rejected the socialist label, so adherents have no stake in the definition of socialism.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Georgists commonly treat natural monopolies such as water and transit as suited to public ownership, but the sources opened here do not detail this; inferred.

second-chamber.rationale: Georgism has no doctrine on legislative structure.

municipal-property.rationale: George held that producers keep private ownership of their products and improvements while only land rent is collected, so the means of production stay privately owned.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The movement suggests collecting rent locally but has no doctrine of confederal assemblies; inferred as neutral.

family-wage.rationale: George held wages are set by the free product of labour once rent is taken, not by a household standard, but some adherents sympathise with the idea.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Geolibertarian adherents lean toward lighter regulation, but George never addressed it; inferred from classical-liberal outlook.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: George did not address it, and adherents are split between public funding and leaving it to private effort.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The libertarian-leaning strand favours financial privacy, but George never addressed it; inferred.

online-anonymity.rationale: Classical-liberal and geolibertarian adherents favour free speech and privacy; this is an inference since George never addressed it.

person-over-state.rationale: George grounded his case in each person's equal right to land and to their own product, which implies the state serves individuals; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: George argued from Christian and moral premises, as in his open letter to Pope Leo XIII, and saw justice as serving moral and spiritual life.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Georgism has no doctrine on the legal basis of regional autonomy.

gm-crops.rationale: The movement never addressed genetic engineering, and adherents do not share a view.

dense-cities.rationale: Georgists commonly argue a land value tax encourages compact development and discourages sprawl and speculation, though George did not address the environment; inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: George's founding premise is equal rights for all people, which sits against organising politically by race; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Georgism takes no position on pride in ancestry.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: George favoured free trade and peace and opposed monopoly privilege and imperial adventure; inferred from that outlook.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Georgism is individualist and cosmopolitan, favoring free trade and equal rights over ethnic or linguistic nationhood; inferred, as George did not address it.

communal-electorates.rationale: George held equal individual rights and a liberal democracy, so separate religious electorates would run against his view; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Its free-trade, anti-war outlook sees conflict as the product of land monopoly and privilege, not foreign plots; inferred.

free-public-college.rationale: George wanted the benefits of land rent shared by all and favored public provision of education; the sources do not address tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The movement's overview lists charges on resource use and pollution rents among the things to be taxed, consistent with its tax-based approach.

future-generations.rationale: George's claim that every person has an equal right to the earth, since land is common property, extends to those born later.

women-distinct-values.rationale: George backed women's suffrage on equal-rights grounds, not on a claim of distinct values; inferred.

arms-reduction.rationale: George expected government to need smaller police and armies once the land question was settled, and traced wars to land struggles.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Its liberal democratic outlook favors public accountability; the sources do not discuss secret treaties.

capital-controls.rationale: Georgism pairs the land tax with free trade, tariffs rejected, and no taxes on capital, so state control of capital flows runs against it.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from George's view of government as cooperative administration with a shrinking police and army.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the classical-liberal outlook, which treats law-abiding service as the default, though George opposed war and armies.

collective-bargaining.rationale: George backed workers' rights but doubted strikes and unions as the remedy for poverty; adherents are split and the sources do not settle it.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from George's view that taxing labour is wrong and that land rent, not wage top-ups, should fund the public good.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the classical-liberal outlook of the movement, which favours limited and restrained government finance.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: George's free trade helps poorer countries but he proposed no restructuring of international rules; adherents are not clearly for or against.

smash-state-machine.rationale: George sought reform through ordinary democratic politics and a liberal democratic society, leaving land in private hands.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal outlook and its claim that land reform would let free arrangements flourish.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Georgists want the rent of natural resources, including pollution rents, reflected in public revenue, though George kept land distinct from capital.

sacred-nation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the classical-liberal and individualist outlook.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the view that reform should come through land rent, with labour and its products left untaxed.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a movement that attributes inequality to private land monopoly, not to regions exploiting regions.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from George's natural-rights reasoning that every person has an equal right to land and to the products of labour.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the classical-liberal preference for private media over state funding.

religions-one-truth.rationale: George wrote in a theistic, moral-law vein but did not claim all religions share one truth; adherents are split.

farm-price-support.rationale: Georgists favour free trade and oppose special privilege; they would tax land rent rather than guarantee crop prices.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic for George; he wanted armies shrunk, but modern adherents are split on unilateral disarmament.

workers-own-party.rationale: George stood for mayor of New York in 1886 on a labor-backed ticket and the movement sought independent political action for reform.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the classical-liberal view that rights over one's own person are protected from coercion.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: George backed women's suffrage and equal rights to land for all people; equal inheritance is inferred from that.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Georgism has no position on language classification.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Georgists would charge for use of natural resources, including pollution rents, while geolibertarians favour courts; adherents are split.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: George envisaged liberal democratic government as cooperative administration with no formal place for hereditary leaders; inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Georgists favour charging for natural resource use rather than overriding liberty, and adherents vary between geolibertarians and social-democratic Georgists.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from classical-liberal support for civil liberties and due process, and George's view of shrinking police power.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: George favoured free movement of people alongside free trade apart from his views on Chinese immigration; a state requirement is not part of the outlook.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the classical-liberal emphasis on voluntary association, with George defending free workers' combinations.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that adherents are split, as the movement has no position on voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal, equal-rights outlook; George did not write on this question.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred from George's faith in democratic self-government and equal political rights, though he cared more about economic justice than electoral procedure.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the classical-liberal and libertarian lean of modern Georgists.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the movement's liberty-centred outlook and distrust of state power.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Georgists would replace taxes and some welfare with land rent, and some adherents would return surplus rent as a citizen's dividend; inferred, as the cash-payment form is not universal.

women-suffrage.rationale: George backed women's suffrage and equal rights as a corollary of equal natural rights.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the secular-liberal outlook, though George himself was religious and wrote to the Pope.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by George; inferred from the movement's equal-natural-rights principle and modern adherents' mainstream views.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from the limited-government, classical-liberal lean; adherents would prefer to remove land privilege over creating new agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: George held that land and natural resources belong equally to all and rejected first-claim title, which is why land rent should go to the community.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: George never addressed international criminal law; classical-liberal and geolibertarian strands differ on it, so adherents are split.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: George was a religious deist who cited Christian moral teaching, as in his letter to Pope Leo XIII, but did not hold literal inerrancy; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: George never addressed group self-government arrangements; inferred as no clear Georgist position.

defend-planned-state.rationale: George opposed state ownership of capital and a planned economy, so defending one is inferred to be unlikely; he did not address bureaucratic socialist states.

indirect-election.rationale: George advocated democratic reforms and direct government by the people; inferred, not discussed in these sources.

national-church-status.rationale: George's equal-rights principle and his critique of monopoly privilege oppose legal privilege for any church; he took up church matters in the Pope Leo letter.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: George never addressed ethnic minority territories; adherents are split and it is not discussed.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed by George; liberal self-determination suggests support but it is not stated by the sources.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not addressed by George or the movement, and anachronistic; no position can be inferred.

simple-living.rationale: George's goal was abundance from ending land monopoly and wealth for all; he did not call for limited needs.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Georgism pairs equal rights to land with free movement and free trade, so restricting settlement is inferred to be disfavored.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed by George; classical liberals and geolibertarians are split on conscription.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Georgism is universalist: land belongs to all people equally, not to a nation as an ancestral inheritance; inferred from this principle.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: George's liberal rights-based outlook gives no room for killing without trial; inferred, he never addressed it.

close-ties-china.rationale: George backed free trade with all countries but never addressed alignment with China; inferred and neutral.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from George's universalist, free-trade outlook, which does not single out kin abroad for state protection.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: George's founding claim is that land belongs equally to all, so those who hold it owe the community its rental value.

self-ownership.rationale: George holds that each person owns what they produce by their own labour, the counterpart of common ownership of land.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The single tax would replace taxes on labor, capital and trade, which includes consumption taxes on everyday goods.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Georgists favour universal returns such as a citizen's dividend more than means-tested aid; inferred, and geolibertarians would shrink spending.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from George's democratic, classical-liberal outlook; he campaigned through parties and movements rather than bypassing them.

no-business-privileges.rationale: George opposed monopoly privilege, with land monopoly the chief case, and wanted privileges abolished.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the movement's classical-liberal outlook; George never addressed denominational parties.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred: George welcomed progress and material improvement and gave no weight to ancestral tradition.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the movement's liberal, equal-rights outlook; George did not address divorce.

national-resource-control.rationale: George held resources belong to all people equally, which is neither national nor foreign control; adherents differ and the issue is inferred.

missingStatements.text: Land and natural resources belong to everyone in common, so whoever holds them owes the community their rental value.
missingStatements.rationale: George's founding claim is that land must be made common property by taking its rent, and this common-ownership premise, shared or rejected by many other ideologies, is broader than any tax policy.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by land-value-tax, which already identifies Georgism.

notes: Georgists split between a 'single tax limited' strand that would raise only what government needs and an 'unlimited' strand that would take all land rent, often returning surplus as a dividend. George's own 1869 opposition to Chinese immigration is not shared by the modern movement, so immigration answers follow the current mainstream. Most social-issue answers are inferred because the ideology is primarily economic.
